page.layout: One column of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin. No left margin notes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: & ecclesiam Dei pene deficere, pro ea, quâ erant fidei infirmitate, putare: solatur Deus fideles, eo quod ipsorum semen ramos extensurum per progressus aquarum, gentium vocatione esset. Ita Isai. 54. 1, 2, 3. &c. Gal. 4. 27. Esai. 2. v. 1, 2, 3. dixerim vix legisse scripturas qui assereret non esse vocationem gentium, judæis solatio. 5. Resp. Re-s. Resp.mon. lib. Promissio ad totum populum dirigitur: Remonst. at gratia ista peculiaris non ad totum populum pertinet: denique si ad paucos tantum quosdam, ex gentibus nominatum à Deo ab æterno electos promissio pertinere dicatur, quænam erat solatio hæc qua Israelem Deus vult erigere contra metum &c. R. 1.
Communi hac cantilenâ nihil frigidius: an ex Dei intentione & decreto promissiones evangelicæ ad reprobos spectent, vos dicite, id nos negamus.
2. Solamen non mediocre est electis promissio gratiæ determinantis: reprobis nihil in scripturis solatio esse dicimus: quid illis cum pace, cum solatio, cum spiritus sancti gaudio?

3. Dicite ex conscientiis ecquid solatii sit ullis filiis Adami, ex promissione illius gratiæ, adversus omnes hujus vitæ, mundi, peccati, Diaboli, ærumnarum omnium, mortis, & infernalis terroris, insultus & tentationes, quâ posita fieri potest ut omnes in æternum exitium ruant, & illis omnes tentationes cedant in extremum malum, liquidem ipsi, uti liberè possent, voluntatem flectant ad assentiendum tentationi. Certe hic in libero arbitrio sive in nova Dea contingentiâ aut for-tunâ,

page.notes: Page number read as "415"; the final digit is a worn form and is marked [?]. The printed "ff" is transcribed as "ss" (Promissio, Dissertatio-style spelling) and long s as plain s. The marginal "s. Resp." and "Remonst." are small italic notes; I read them as shown. Italic passages are marked with <i>; the reference "Isai." is italic in print. The line "tunâ," is the completion of the hyphenated word "for-tunâ," and is kept in the text, not as a catchword.
